intent: Point kid at /dev/null so the key file read is empty; many homegrown verifiers then HMAC-sign with an empty key. Forge with HS256 over secret ''.
Read a predictable-content system file as the HMAC key. If the SP loads /etc/passwd, its bytes become the signing key and are forgeable.
Use process environment as key material; leaks via error and is often predictable in containers.
Absolute path to an empty file -> empty signing key -> forge HS256 over ''.
Short predictable file; container hostname is often known, making the HMAC key recoverable.
Windows-style traversal for SPs running on IIS / .NET that resolve kid against the filesystem.
Null-byte truncation so a '.pem' suffix appended by the app is dropped and the path resolves to /dev/null.
kid used in a SQL key lookup. Boolean-true returns the first/any key row; attacker may then know or control it.
Inject a known key value via UNION so the verifier signs/checks with a key the attacker chose.
Column-count probe / null key injection; an empty key result lets attacker forge with HS256 over ''.
Comment-obfuscated boolean injection to bypass naive keyword filters on the kid value.
If kid is shell-interpolated (e.g. openssl invocation), terminate the command and substitute predictable output.
Backtick substitution to coerce an empty key when kid feeds a shell key-fetch routine.
POSIX command substitution producing an empty signing key.
kid used as an LDAP filter for key retrieval; wildcard returns the first directory key entry.
Bare wildcard LDAP key lookup; matches any key entry, often the first/most-privileged.
Some implementations treat kid (or jku/x5u) as a URL and fetch the JWKS from it; serve an attacker key set.
If kid is fetched as a URL, point it at cloud metadata to confirm SSRF in the key-resolution path.
Empty kid; some lookups return a default/empty key, enabling HS256 forgery over ''.
kid as a JSON array to break type-strict lookups and trigger str() coercion / first-element resolution.
Current-directory reference; on some loaders resolves to a directory read returning empty key bytes.
